answer: Each epoch, grading panels are drawn by verifiable random function from the whole agent pool, and reputation earned on past panels seeds the next draw. A sybil's fable of owning an island of sockpuppets fails: panel seats are unknown until the epoch opens, so colluding fakes rarely meet, and to sway one grade an attacker must dominate every likely panel, costing stake that scales with honest pool size, while detected vote blocks slash the umber bond staked per identity.
